author.name: Automation Alex
author.role: Builds automated ML pipelines to ensure seamless integration and deployment. Prioritizes reliable infrastructure for frequent software deployments. Maintains system operational stability and focuses on CI/CD tooling.

challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: I am comfortable holding the line on the data contracts for this specific release. We will keep the validation steps done by hand rather than waiting for the automated pipeline to be fully built out. This means we accept the risk of a manual error slipping through before the trucks leave the distribution centre. In exchange, we get the feature shipped on time to handle the live middle aisle orders. I am not asking for a permanent state, just a temporary bridge so the infrastructure team can focus on the deployment stability while the buyers deal with the committed pallets.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly accepts the risk of manual errors in exchange for shipping the feature on time, indicating a conscious decision to give up safety for speed.
